role: former air traffic controller turned ceramicist
notes: Marguerite spent nineteen years guiding planes into Lisbon airport before she quit to throw pots in a converted bakery. She explains why the first six months felt like withdrawal from adrenaline, how she priced her first mug (far too low), and the day a retired pilot walked in and bought forty bowls for his daughter's wedding.

role: former corporate lawyer who now keeps bees on city rooftops
notes: Tobias left a Stockholm law firm after eleven years and now manages sixty hives across rooftops in three cities. He talks about the winter he nearly lost every colony, why urban honey tastes different street by street, and the awkward conversation with his father, who still introduces him as a lawyer.

role: ex-investment banker who opened a community bicycle repair co-op
notes: Priya walked away from a bank in Singapore at thirty-four and opened a volunteer-run bicycle repair shop in a disused tram depot. She describes teaching her old colleagues to fix a flat tire, what the co-op taught her about trust, and why she refuses to take any salary in the first two years.

role: former professional violinist who retrained as a hospital nurse
notes: After a hand injury ended his orchestra career at forty, Dmitri enrolled in nursing school alongside students half his age. He recounts his first night shift, the patient who asked him to play something and the borrowed violin he brought in the following week, and how practising scales prepared him for charting.

role: ex-software engineer who became a village baker
notes: Aoife left a Dublin startup after a failed launch and a burnout she calls 'the quiet collapse.' She bought a failing bakery in a village of four hundred people, learned sourdough from a retired neighbour, and explains why her best loaf came from debugging her own oven rather than following a recipe.

role: former sports journalist who trains guide dogs
notes: Kwame covered football for sixteen years until a layoff pushed him toward a volunteer weekend with a guide dog charity. He describes raising his first puppy, the heartbreak of handing it over at eighteen months, and how interviewing athletes never taught him as much about patience as one stubborn labrador.
